obtained.how: open-access (CC BY 4.0) full text as Europe PMC's JATS XML of PMC12358046 (the publisher's PDF and the PMC pages refuse scripts); the text is one 'web page', so locations give the section and paragraph

bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the article's front matter in the XML
bibliography.note: Journal of Plankton Research 47(5), article fbaf035 (Sep–Oct 2025; online 17 Aug 2025); authors and title match. Figures were not read (the XML carries captions only); every value checked here is in the text

claims.claim: Lake Simoncouche's under-ice biomass in 2020–21 was 35 % L. minutus, 15 % C. scutifer, 12 % Kellicottia, 11 % Daphnia and 8 % Bosmina (values read from figures)
claims.location: web page, Results, paragraph on zooplankton taxa (after Fig. 2); repeated in the Discussion
claims.quote: Leptodiaptomus minutus (35%), Cyclops scutifer (15%), Kellicottia longispina (12%), Daphnia sp. (11%)
claims.conditions: shares of total zooplankton biomass (dry weight from length–DW regressions) over all six dates, autumn overturn (13 Nov 2020) to spring overturn (19 Apr 2021), five depths at the 8-m deep point; Bosmina sp. 8 %
claims.note: the values are stated in the text, not read from figures: drop 'values read from figures' for these. The shares include the two open-water overturn dates. The source says six taxa made 89 % but names only five (summing to 81 %)

claims.claim: M. edax, Diaphanosoma, Holopedium and Leptodora were absent
claims.quote: were entirely absent from the water column, including the autumn and spring shoulder seasons
claims.conditions: taxa that make > 15 % of the summer crustacean production in the lake; absent on all six dates (spelled 'Mecocyclops' and 'Diaphosoma' in the source)

claims.claim: nauplii were about 34 % of biomass at melt
claims.location: web page, Results, paragraph on community structure (after Fig. 3)
claims.quote: contributing ~ 34% to total community biomass in the melting season
claims.conditions: copepod nauplii as a share of total zooplankton biomass (rotifers, cladocerans, copepods), melting-season sample of 12 Apr 2021; nauplii 'nearly absent' in early winter

claims.claim: egg-bearing Daphnia went from none in late winter to 21 % at overturn
claims.location: web page, Results, paragraph on reproduction (Fig. 5)
claims.quote: with ~21% of the active Daphnia sp. population bearing eggs
claims.conditions: percent of the Daphnia population; egg production 'completely stopping in late winter' (23 Mar), ~6 % just before ice-off, ~21 % at spring overturn (19 Apr)

claims.claim: Kellicottia and K. cochlearis are prominent under the ice at Lake Simoncouche
claims.location: web page, Results, paragraphs on zooplankton taxa and community structure
claims.quote: K. cochlearis was the most abundant rotifer species accounting for 20% of total zooplankton biomass
claims.conditions: K. cochlearis 20 % of total biomass in early winter, ~9 % at ice-off; K. longispina 12 % of total biomass over the study, most present at 7 m

claims.claim: Daphnia make ephippia: 13–27 % of females carry them in autumn (Cáceres 1998; Boulianne et al. 2025)
claims.source_value: 27 % of the Daphnia population at the autumn overturn (13 Nov 2020, open water) and 13 % in early winter (14 Dec, under ice); percentages of the population, not of females
claims.location: web page, Results, paragraph on reproduction (Fig. 5 caption: 'percentage of the respective population density')
claims.quote: 27% and 13% of the Daphnia sp. population, respectively bearing ephippia
claims.conditions: Lake Simoncouche, Québec, 2020–21; whole water column
claims.note: the 13 % is an under-ice value, and both are shares of all Daphnia (juveniles included), not of females; Cáceres 1998 not checked here

claims.claim: the copepod field's naupliar share of its biomass is 34 % at ice-melt (Simoncouche, Boulianne et al. 2025; L. minutus lays from February, its nauplii hatch in March)
claims.source_value: nauplii were ~34 % of TOTAL zooplankton biomass (rotifers and cladocerans included) in the melting season; their share of copepod biomass alone would be higher. The source does not give February laying or March hatching for L. minutus
claims.location: web page, Results, paragraphs on community structure and on reproduction
claims.quote: contributing ~ 34% to total community biomass in the melting season
claims.conditions: melting-season sample, 12 Apr 2021; egg-bearing L. minutus 28 % in the melting season and 44 % at spring overturn
claims.note: the code uses a share of the whole community as a share of the copepod field. The February/March timing is Cooley 1973's (credited to Cooley in §3.3.5), not Boulianne's

tried.note: OUP refuses scripts (the article is open access)

notes: Other values: Lake Simoncouche 0.8 km², mean depth 2.2 m, max 8 m, TDP 7.2 µg/L, residence 50 d, ice 5–6 months (43 cm max in 2020–21); under ice the water was 1.3 °C at the surface in early winter rising to 4.8 °C, 4–5 °C at the bottom; bottom O₂ fell to 2.5 % saturation in mid-winter; chlorophyll-a 0.35–2.3 µg/L under ice, ~3.7 at the overturns; 18–22 zooplankton taxa per under-ice date (14–22 over all six dates; Table II); biomass at 7 m about three times that at 0–1.5 m; Bosmina egg-bearers ~8 % in late winter, 14 % at spring overturn; Kellicottia and Keratella > 20 % fecund in the melting season and spring overturn. Absolute biomass is in Fig. 3 only (mg DW m⁻³), not read.
